cards.meaning: a testimony, account, or narrative -- what someone says happened, given as a record
cards.example: Sa kanyang salaysay sa Senado ngayong Martes, inamin ni Ortonio na siya mismo ang tumakip sa kulang na 150,000 pisong liquidation noong 2024.
cards.exampleMeaning: In his testimony to the Senate this Tuesday, Ortonio admitted he personally covered a 150,000-peso liquidation shortfall from 2024.
cards.note: The standard word for a formal spoken or written account -- what a witness gives on the stand, or what a report tells you happened. More neutral and documentary than 'kwento' (a story, which can be casual or embellished); 'salaysay' is the word you'd use for sworn testimony or a news dispatch, not a bedtime story.
cards.tiesTo: Duterte impeachment trial Day 18 -- Ortonio declared hostile witness, testifies to covering a 150,000-peso liquidation gap

cards.meaning: a tightening -- policy, rules, or conditions being made stricter
cards.example: Inaasahan ng mga analyst ang isa pang paghihigpit sa patakaran ng BSP tuwing Huwebes, dahil patuloy pa ring mataas ang implasyon.
cards.exampleMeaning: Analysts expect another BSP policy tightening this Thursday, because inflation is still running high.
cards.note: From the root 'higpit' (strictness/tightness) plus the 'pag-hi-' gerund pattern, naming tightening as a deliberate act of policy. The finance-desk word for a central bank raising rates or squeezing conditions -- distinct from 'paghina' (a weakening), which describes something losing strength rather than being reined in on purpose.
cards.tiesTo: BusinessWorld poll: 19 of 24 analysts expect a 25bp BSP hike at Thursday's Aug 27 review

cards.meaning: only if ... then -- states a necessary condition, without which the result cannot happen
cards.example: 只有房地产市场真正企稳，央行才有可能进一步放松货币政策。
cards.examplePinyin: zhǐ yǒu fáng dì chǎn shì chǎng zhēn zhèng qǐ wěn, yāng háng cái yǒu kě néng jìn yī bù fàng sōng huò bì zhèng cè
cards.exampleMeaning: Only if the property market genuinely stabilizes will the central bank be able to further loosen monetary policy.
cards.note: 书面语 (formal register), the standard connective for a strict necessary condition -- distinct from 一旦……就…… (once ... then), which marks a trigger that immediately produces a result. 只有……才…… says the opposite logical shape: nothing else will get you there, this is the one precondition that unlocks it -- the phrase a policy analyst reaches for, not a casual conversation.
cards.tiesTo: China's 10Y bond yield falling to a 13-month low as investors bet the PBOC won't truly ease further until growth stabilizes

cards.meaning: to deviate from, diverge from -- move away from an expected path or relationship
cards.example: 债市持续走强，股市却屡创新高，两者的走势已经明显背离。
cards.examplePinyin: zhài shì chí xù zǒu qiáng, gǔ shì què lǚ chuàng xīn gāo, liǎng zhě de zǒu shì yǐ jīng míng xiǎn bèi lí
cards.exampleMeaning: Bonds keep strengthening while equities keep hitting new highs -- the two have clearly diverged.
cards.note: 书面语 (formal, financial-register), an abstract verb that collocates with 趋势 (a trend) or 走势 (a market movement) -- it carries a sense that something has broken away from where it should track. A near-synonym of 分化 (to split/differentiate), which is the more neutral word for a group splitting into subgroups; 背离 specifically flags two things that used to move together now pulling apart.
cards.tiesTo: China's bond yields at a 13-month low even as AI-linked equities keep ripping to multi-year highs -- the two-speed decoupling
